name: Allendale County Courthouse
unique: A 1920s courthouse with a copper dome and columns that was gutted by fire in 1998 and rebuilt inside the original shell, still the handsomest building in a county of 8,000 people.
buzz: People stop for the photo and end up reading the veterans memorial on the lawn. The restoration is the local point of pride.

name: Red Bluff Lodge
unique: A full service lodge on the Savannah River bluff with deer, hog and turkey hunts, a shooting range, kayak trips and naturalist tours, sleeping up to 22.
buzz: It is a hunting lodge first, but the kayaking and naturalist trips are open to anyone who books. Meals are included and the river bluff is the view.

name: Swallow Savannah Cemetery
unique: A country graveyard in the woods where a log church stood in 1815, still in use, with tilted stones and Spanish moss and no building left to explain it.
buzz: Quiet and a little overgrown, which is the atmosphere people come for. Look for the oldest markers near the back.

name: Allendale Farmers Market
unique: A small town market with produce, plants, dairy and a playground, where the whole county seems to show up on a Saturday morning.
buzz: It is tiny and genuine, with special events through the season. Go early because the greens go first.

name: Peach Tree 23 Yard Sale
unique: A 30 mile yard sale along Highway 23 through peach country, with hundreds of tables, boiled peanuts, old tools and things nobody can identify.
buzz: Bring cash, a truck and patience. The early morning is the good stuff and the church barbecue is the lunch stop.

name: Ridge Spring Harvest Festival
unique: A one day harvest festival in a peach town with a parade, cane grinding, gospel music and a contest for the best sweet potato pie.
buzz: Small, crowded and worth the drive. Parking is in fields and the pie table sells out before noon.

name: Persimmon Hill Golf Course
unique: A nine hole country course cut through pines and peach orchards, with greens fees low enough to play twice and a clubhouse that sells sandwiches.
buzz: Nobody pretends it is Augusta, and that is the charm. The fairways are wide, the pace is slow, and visitors are welcome.

name: Lake Murray, Saluda Shore
unique: The quiet western shore of a 50,000 acre lake, with public ramps, fishing coves and sunsets that pull people off the road.
buzz: The lake is the local summer. Rentals and ramps are on the Saluda side, and the striper fishing is the quiet draw.

name: Skydive Carolina
unique: A large drop zone with tandem jumps from 14,000 feet over the Piedmont, plus accelerated freefall training if you want to go alone.
buzz: The outfit runs a tight operation and the instructors talk nervous first timers down. Video packages cost extra and the landing field is easy to find.

name: Fish Dam Ford
unique: A Revolutionary War crossing on the Broad River where Sumter's men surprised a British camp, now a quiet boat ramp and shoal with a marker and no crowds.
buzz: The history takes ten minutes and the river takes the rest. Local anglers will tell you where the shoal is if you ask.

name: South Carolina Cotton Museum
unique: A museum of cotton from seed to bale, with a gin, a sharecropper cabin, the Lee County veterans room and the story of how one crop shaped the whole Pee Dee.
buzz: The machinery is the hit with kids and the veteran exhibits suprise adults. Allow ninety minutes.

name: Button Museum
unique: The collection of Dalton Stevens, the Button King, who covered a car, a coffin and a suit in buttons, with the car parked outside and thousands of buttons inside.
buzz: It is exactly as strange as it sounds and the family is proud of it. Call ahead, because hours depend on the family.

name: Kreepy Hollow Haunted Attraction
customer: Teens, young adults, families with older kids
unique: A woods walk haunted trail on a farm outside Bishopville, built and performed by local volunteers, with a hayride and a midway of food stalls.
buzz: Community theater with chainsaws, and people say the trail is longer than expected. Check the weather and wear closed shoes.

name: Artesian Wells at Lee State Park
unique: Four flowing artesian wells drilled by the CCC, still running, where people fill jugs with cold mineral water in the middle of a state park.
buzz: Locals swear by the water and bring jugs. It is a five minute stop that pairs with the park trails and the CCC stonework.

name: Fort Motte Battle Site
unique: The site of a 1781 siege where Marion's men burned a British post by firing flaming arrows onto its roof, marked today by a roadside sign and a quiet field.
buzz: There is almost nothing to see but the marker, and that is the point for a certain kind of traveler. Read the story first or it is just a field.

name: Withlacoochee Park
unique: A wooded city park on the edge of Marion with a pond, a campground, picnic shelters and a walking loop under oaks and pines.
buzz: A locals' park with cheap campsites and good shade. The pond is for fishing, not swimming.

name: Marion Hike-Bike Trail
unique: A paved greenway along Bobby Gerald Parkway that connects the downtown grid to the parks, flat enough for a beach cruiser and long enough for a real ride.
buzz: Newish, smooth and rarely busy. It is the easiest way to see the town without fighting traffic.

name: Foxes Tales Bookstore
unique: An independent bookshop on Main Street with used and new titles, local authors and a children's corner, in a town that has lost most of its chain stores.
buzz: The kind of shop people drive to on purpose. Staff recommendations are handwritten and good.

name: Lake Greenwood State Park
unique: A CCC park on a peninsula in Lake Greenwood, with stone picnic shelters, a swimming area, a boat ramp and cabins overlooking the water.
buzz: The lake is the draw and the CCC stonework is a bonus. Summer weekends are busy, but the campground is quiet on weeknights.

name: Greenwood Museum
unique: A county museum with Native American pottery, a railroad room and changing art exhibits, in a converted post office downtown.
buzz: Small but well done, and free or nearly so. The railroad and Native American rooms are the strongest.

name: Festival of Flowers
unique: A week long civic festival with topiary displays, a flower show, a street dance and a concert series in the uptown square.
buzz: The topiaries are the photo op and the street dance is the local party. Check the schedule because events are spread across the week.

name: Newberry County Museum
unique: A county museum in the old courthouse area with Native American artifacts, cotton mill records and the story of Newberry College during Reconstruction.
buzz: Volunteers run it and know the families. Call first, because hours are short.

name: Lynch's Woods Park
unique: A 270 acre park of old growth hardwood and a five mile trail along a creek, one of the few places in the Piedmont where the trees were never cleared.
buzz: The trail is well marked and rolling, with big trees and quiet. It is a real hike, not a sidewalk loop.

name: Andrew Jackson State Park
unique: The birthplace of Andrew Jackson, with a museum, a one room schoolhouse, a lake and a sculpture of the boy who would become president.
buzz: The museum is small and the grounds are pretty, with a lake for fishing and a trail for kids. The Jackson story is told without hero worship.

name: Lancaster County Courthouse
unique: An 1828 courthouse that survived Sherman's march because the town surrendered, with a copper roof and a monument to the local men who fought.
buzz: The story of why the town was spared is better than the building, and locals tell it well. Look up at the cupola.
